decision: One owned Chromium-family browser per registered computer, bound to the SAME durable ComputerRegistry home/leases/authority as the native worker computer; no external Dot supervisor is required and none is implied

identity.profile_root: ComputerRegistry HomeManifest.browser_profile joined with the service's profile_scope directory; never a parallel path, never a user profile, never caller-supplied

profile_scope.public: Login-less research profile. The only scope a worker relay may open. Confinement: navigation targets and every intercepted in-browser request (including redirects) must resolve to publicly routable http(s) origins; private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, ULA, and metadata ranges are denied before connecting. A URL labeled public never makes a persisted profile public.
profile_scope.private: Authenticated profile for owner-driven takeover and Host-conversation use. Never served to a subscription-native (public-route) worker; never promoted into a cloud worker session. Captured bundles include both scopes; capture/restore never starts a browser.
profile_scope.separation: One active browser service per computer declaring exactly one scope; switching scope is an explicit attach at the next grant revision. The v1 persistent profile has exactly one concurrent writer per computer.

registry_commands.attach_browser: Authenticated Ghost command: attaches the service at the binding epoch; replacement requires expected_revision and advances the grant revision by exactly one; refused while a browser lease is active; capabilities must exactly match the backend's offered set and acceptance stays inside the operator-trusted set
registry_commands.detach_browser: Fences the gate: state revoked, grant revision advanced, every active browser lease revoked immediately; the binding epoch and worker home are untouched
registry_commands.lease: kind=browser is granted only through a current attached service (active, binding epoch, backend configured+available+trusted); single writer per computer; native process/collect leases still require atomic acquire_worker_home
registry_commands.typed_helpers: acquire_browser_lease / browser_lease_is_current / release_browser_lease mirror the worker-home helpers: single transaction, no resurrection of released or revoked leases, per-operation currency revalidation
registry_commands.revoke: Computer revoke fences the attached service and all leases in the same transaction; return is only through explicit re-attach at the next epoch

runtime_lifecycle.accept_runtime: Explicit per-epoch acceptance cross-checked against operator-probed RuntimeFacts (kind + executable sha256) registered at Host/worker startup; a command payload can never attest a runtime
runtime_lifecycle.recreate_idle_stop: Refused while process or collection leases are active (browser leases belong to the runtime being stopped); without acceptance the plan stays warning runtime_not_accepted with executed:false; with acceptance the plan is an authorization (authorized:true, executed:false) that a lifecycle executor must confirm via lifecycle_effect against the exact authorization receipt
runtime_lifecycle.effects: Executed only by the process owning the runtime; crash between effect and completion re-executes on retry (idle_stop idempotent, recreate restarts); completed lifecycles never re-execute

worker_path.grant: GuestRunnerConfig optional browser section; operator-pinned executable digest verified by probe; the Host browser section and the worker grant must declare the identical executable or startup fails
worker_path.tool: Scoped host tool `browser` advertised only when the worker grant exists; registered host tools become exactly publish_artifact (+browser); the frozen eleven-builtin proof is unchanged
worker_path.observations: navigate/read/snapshot/screenshot only; confined to the public profile scope with request interception
worker_path.actions: click/type/key/scroll require an exact owner approval: the worker proposes the precise arguments digest bound to its execution, computer, and epoch; the owner approves or denies through the control plane; execution revalidates approved state, digest, browser lease, worker-home leases, and authority epoch before the effect, and records the effect against the digest; stale proposals can never be approved
worker_path.lease_binding: The browser lease identity is worker:<execution_id> at the spec authority epoch; stale epoch, revoked binding, detached service, or disabled dispatch reject before any execution or cached replay
worker_path.settlement: Settled, collected executions release the browser lease with the worker home; unknown cleanup keeps both for explicit reconciliation

human_handoff.take: Owner-only control-plane verb (owner control token; model callers cannot reach it): pauses agent automation, advances the control epoch, invalidates all observations, records a handoff id
human_handoff.release: Owner-only verb: resume-pending until a fresh observation replaces the invalidated one; stale refs and stale snapshot ids are refused
human_handoff.isolation: Worker read/navigation and owner takeover are separate authorities; config capabilities never substitute for the owner's live decision; no control token or CDP endpoint is ever shared with the guest

recovery.capture: Bundles capture the master registry ledger (role computer-registry) plus per-computer home/browser presence facts; manifest computers must exist in the captured ledger
recovery.restore: Restored browser profiles stay unallocated until explicit computer rebind and browser service attach at the new authority epoch; old restored leases never resurrect
recovery.rebind: ghost computers rebind advances the binding epoch exactly once with the expected grant revision; dispatch re-enable (ghost lifetime accept --confirm) refuses until every binding is active at the new epoch with runtime acceptance and the operator confirms

verification: two Ghosts under one master registry, each with an owned persistent profile that survives browser stop/restart
single-writer refusal across Host session, worker execution, and operator CLI
revoke/detach/epoch-advance fences live writers before their next effect
public-route worker cannot open a private profile and cannot reach non-public hosts, including via redirects
worker non-observational actions execute only after an exact, current, owner-approved proposal
recreate/idle_stop execute only with probe-matched per-epoch runtime acceptance; authorization and effect receipts are durable and replay-safe
restore-then-rebind yields a live fleet with dispatch off until explicit acceptance; no old execution replays
